messages:
Maria Ops: Heads up - since last night we've seen intermittent packet loss between gpu-node-7 and gpu-node-12 in us-east-2b during backfills. ~0.5-2% packet drops observed, manifests as slightly longer GRPC p99 and some backfill retries.
Ryan Infra: Confirmed, saw spikes aligned with backfill windows. Overlay (Geneve) egress counters tick up then clear. Not seeing underlay congestion.
Sofia SRE: Any MTU mismatch? Also can you paste `ip -d link` for the geneve interface and `ethtool -k` on the NIC?
Maria Ops: Quick dump attached below:
```
$ ip link show dev geneve0
4: geneve0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1450 qdisc noop state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
$ ethtool -k ens5 | sed -n '1,20p'
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
large-receive-offload: on
large-send-offload: on
```
Maria Ops: Underlay MTU is 9000 on hosts, but geneve MTU set to 1450 by CNI.
Kai Platform: That MTU/Geneve size difference is expected, but weird that only happens during backfill windows. Could be burst-induced offload bug on mlx5 driver.
Ryan Infra: I ran `tcpdump -i geneve0 -n -c 1000` during a backfill and saw occasional fragment/ICMP frag-needed logs on the nodes. Packet sizes around 2500B after encapsulation.
Sofia SRE: Can you share `dmesg` for NIC err logs? Also check `ip -s link show geneve0` counters for rx/tx errors.
Maria Ops: dmesg tail: "mlx5_core 0000:65:00.0: XDP: driver rx Q error" and some TSO errors. `ip -s link show geneve0` shows small burst of dropped packets on TX side when loss observed.
Kai Platform: Quick mitigation: disable LSO/TSO on the host for the interface on one canary node and re-run a backfill. Command:
```
ethtool -K ens5 tx off tso off gso off
```
Ryan Infra: Did that on gpu-node-12 canary. Backfill completed with no packet loss and p99 latency came down ~120ms -> 85ms. :tada:
Sofia SRE: Sounds like NIC offload + encapsulation path is mishandling large segments. We should confirm driver version and kernel. What's the mlx5 version and kernel?
Maria Ops: Kernel 6.1.21, MLX5 fw 18.29.1000 (from node metadata).
Kai Platform: Known issue? I recall a link about mlx5 LSO + Geneve causing fragmentation/packet drops on certain firmwares. I'll search.
deploy-bot: Incident alert auto-post: overlay-loss-spike us-east-2b 2533209950 -> 2533210020
Ryan Infra: Short-term fix: rolled the ethtool change via a DaemonSet to disable tso/gso on ens5 for GPU pool during backfills. Applied 01:12 UTC.
Maria Ops: Patch DS YAML snippet: `hostNetwork: true` + `command: ["/bin/sh","-c","ethtool -K ens5 tso off gso off tx off || true"]`
Sofia SRE: Let's also enable per-node packet sampling (tcpdump rotated) so we can persist a capture when the issue happens. And add a prom alert on Geneve tx_dropped > 10 in 5m.
Kai Platform: Filed INFRA-7198 with vendor and added driver/kernel versions and pcap. Requesting firmware guidance.
Ryan Infra: Long-term plan: test enabling HW segmentation offloads only at underlay where CNI supports offload aware encapsulation (or upgrade driver/firmware). Also consider raising Geneve MTU to 1580 to avoid encapsulated fragments for our typical payloads.
Maria Ops: Note: raising geneve MTU needs CNI bump and coord with kube-proxy tests.
Sofia SRE: For the incident record: root cause likely NIC offload + encapsulation interaction during high-degree concurrent streams (backfill). Mitigation: DS disabling tso/gso pushed, canary nodes show improvement. Next steps: vendor firmware check, kernel/driver upgrades in staging, evaluate controlled re-enable of offloads.
Kai Platform: I'll own the rollout plan for kernel/driver test matrix. Maria, please attach the backfill workload repro steps to INFRA-7198.
Maria Ops: Attached minimal repro: 50 parallel gRPC streams writing 1.5KB payloads between pods on different nodes, run for 10m. Repro reliably triggered loss on canary before DS change.
Sofia SRE: Closing thread for now, opening postmortem if vendor confirms a fix required. Thanks all. :handshake:
